purpose: Identify whether absolute power dependence explains the first SVR pilot's noisy false positives
status: One targeted training-side ablation after the first pilot failed; not adopted
model: Same RBF SVR, removing only the five absolute log-power features
hypothesis: If absolute power dependence causes most transfer false positives, removing these features should reduce FP without merely making all predictions negative
limitations: This ablation was motivated by a noisy training-side result, so it is an exploratory noise-informed design decision
Shape features may still change under additive noise
Architecture is fixed, but selected C can differ because it is independently chosen by nested clean CV
Neither variant is a final outer-test or new-noise validation
